question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $22,$ the additive inverse of $14$ modulo $22$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $14$ modulo $22$ is the integer $0\le x<22$ such that

$$
x+14≡0\,(\text{mod}\,22).
$$

Notice that $-14+14≡0,$ so $x≡-14\,(\text{mod}\,22).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-14 & \,(\text{mod}\,22) \\  & ≡0-14 & \,(\text{mod}\,22) \\  & ≡22-14 & \,(\text{mod}\,22) \\  & ≡8 & \,(\text{mod}\,22)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $14$ modulo $22$ is $8.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
8+14≡22≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,22)
$$

**Note:** The additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
